clue.text: Thread from sack catching tip of briar

indicators.note: the sack word holds the other piece inside it, as if catching it

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here the start of briar

parts.note: the first letter of briar is taken

explanation.surface: A loose strand snagged on a thorny bush is pulled from a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag but is the verb meaning dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibre is a single slender strand, a synonym for a thread.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as a verb, passing mail along to a new address
second meaning: the pack players in a rugby team

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a coach bringing on substitutes, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to redirect it; forwards in rugby are the scrummaging players.

clue.text: Heads of bespoke English fashion industry tailoring suit

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, taken from the next five words

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words spell out the answer

explanation.surface: Custom-made English clothing trade tailors a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like the garment being tailored, but it is the verb meaning be appropriate for.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be fitting or appropriate for someone, as one thing suits another.

indicators.note: back means the cutting word is read in reverse

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it
mining is the work done in a coal pit

explanation.surface: Coal-face labour is being reduced, which proves a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Examining means inspecting or checking closely, the same sense as testing.

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially livestock
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A parent and offspring together turn out some produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark purple plum, a kind of stone fruit.

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a different order

parts.note: the word car is taken as written and its three letters rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a section of a circle, a curved line.

parts.note: to heave is to retch, as when about to be sick

explanation.surface: A way of lifting something heavy and reaching further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heave' suggests hauling a load, but here it is the queasy sense. ST is short for street, a way.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something is to lengthen or extend it.

indicators.note: one is absent, so that letter is taken out of the sound word

parts.note: a noise is a sound
one is I, the Roman numeral; one's here is one is

explanation.surface: A car horn's sound has one element absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn, but it is slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooter is British slang for the nose, especially a large one.

indicators.note: around signals the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: these two words are taken as written and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tossed soil about the low-growing shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergrowth is the dense shrubs and bushes growing beneath taller trees.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold back or desist
second meaning: the repeated chorus of a song

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves as a verb meaning desist and as a noun for the repeated part of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Refrain means abstain as a verb and a recurring lyric section as a noun.

clue.text: Rotters holding right means of payment

indicators.note: the rotters word holds the right letter within it

parts.note: cads and rotters are both old-fashioned words for dishonourable men

explanation.surface: Scoundrels keep hold of the proper way to settle a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit and debit cards are a common method of paying for goods.

clue.text: Recalled part of great Cabaret performance

indicators.note: called back, so the hidden letters are read in reverse order
the answer is only part of the run of letters across these words

parts.note: the last letter of great and first two of Cabaret run together

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a section of a terrific show of Cabaret.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between great and Cabaret, then run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An act is a turn or routine given on stage, so a performance.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in the in thing
Equity is the British trade union for actors and performers

explanation.surface: A well-liked trade union is accused of injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the name of the actors' trade union in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequity is injustice, a lack of fairness in treatment.

indicators.note: the poems piece comes after the college piece

parts.note: uni is short for university
verses are short poems or pieces of poetry

explanation.surface: Poetry written after university explores other realms.
explanation.definitionFit: A universe is a whole world or cosmos, so universes fits worlds.

clue.text: Worships overturned storage chamber during 15th March

indicators.note: during places the reversed chamber within the date word

parts.note: the Ides of March fell on the 15th in the Roman calendar

explanation.surface: Someone venerates a toppled grain store in mid-March.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides was the Roman mid-month date, the 15th in March, remembered for Caesar's assassination.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise is to adore someone excessively, treating them as an object of worship.

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the word studies is taken as written as anagram material
the word hiding is taken as written as anagram material

explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the noun being hidden, but it is the anagram signal on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished person is eminent and celebrated, a synonym of famous.

clue.text: Cut down time in beach cabin at last

parts.note: the shore is the beach

parts.note: the final letter of cabin is taken

explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to reduce its length, to cut it down.

clue.text: Creature with protective covering for flower

parts.note: the fox is one example of a creature
a glove covers and protects the hand

explanation.walkthrough: The plant's name really does join an animal and a hand covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove is a tall garden plant with bell-shaped purple blooms, also called digitalis.

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, so the word is given by its sound

indicators.note: the space word goes around the Northern letter

parts.note: an area is a space or region

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

clue.text: Place of worship where the French returned sailor

indicators.note: turned back, so the French article is read backwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman came back to the place where the French pray.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the table in a church where rites are performed, a focus of worship.

indicators.note: out means the left letter is dropped from the statute word

parts.note: a rule is a law or statute

clue.text: Leader of talented lasses knitted ornamental hangings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as delicate or easily hurt
second meaning: a small boat ferrying people to a larger ship

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a flimsy dinghy, but the two parts are separate meanings.

parts.note: a can and a tin are the same container
